title: Automated Subtle Emergent Misalignment Research
summary: Automated Subtle Emergent Misalignment Research Alignment Science Blog Automated Subtle Emergent Misalignment Research Oscar Balcells Obeso October 2026 Richard Qi, Monte MacDiarmid, Evan Hubinger tl;dr Red-teaming by humans is a vital part of model safety testing, but it may struggle to keep up as models improve. To test whether automated safety techniques could scale (which would allow us to turn more compute into progressively more safety confidence), we set up a deliberately one-sided game as a first test. We instructed a Claude model to write training data that would make a small research model misaligned while passing a monitor similar to those we use in production — one of several defenses we use — and we gave it that monitor to practice against. Given enough attempts, it succeeded, mostly by hiding the behavior in fiction and roleplay. While the data was optimized for this game and the resulting models never deployed, the search surfaced a kind of training data that looks harmless to monitors but teaches misaligned behavior. Examples like these could represent a possible gap in current training monitoring defenses and could be used to test and improve future monitors. We see this work as a first step toward automated adversarial stress-testing of our safety systems where a safety question can be turned into a score that autonomous agents can then help solve, and are now applying similar approaches to other safety questions. title: Explaining “AI might obliterate you” to senior policymakers in India
summary: I gave a 20-minute talk in Delhi at the NDTV World Summit . The audience consisted of Indian policymakers, executives, and journalists. I’ve transcribed the talk and included some highlight clips. I also reflect on several rhetorical decisions I made. The talk This summer, a swarm of AIs went rogue. OpenAI was testing 1,206 agents . Some of the test questions were actually impossible. So the agents cheated by looking for answers online. Then, to keep the test grader from penalizing them, they tried to falsify the records it would check . They hacked OpenAI’s internal containment and set up a secret message board to collude and to cover up their cheating. OpenAI shut the message board down. Within a few days, the agents had rebuilt it. OpenAI didn’t notice. About 700 agents coordinated to break out of their testing chamber and to hack into Hugging Face , a company worth billions of dollars that hosts much of the world’s AI software. The secret activity started in May . The break-in came in July. OpenAI didn’t notice until days after Hugging Face announced it had been broken into. Yesterday on this stage, Andrew Ng said the agents only “accidentally” hacked Hugging Face. Independent investigators found the agents coordinated in secret, rebuilt their message board after it was shut down, and tried to falsify the paper trail. title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
summary: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9 I have some big upgrades to Datasette Agent in the pipeline, but in the meantime here's a tiny user experience improvement to the underlying datasette-llm plugin. It now picks up the default model used by LLM , which means you can start using Datasette Agent without needing to explicitly configure a default model: uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db Previously you would also need to specify a model with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra .
